display.purpose: Page titles, a slab's card name, the DotCard wordmark — anything that should feel collectible-grade.

body.purpose: Default UI copy, list rows, form values.

label.purpose: Uppercase section headers and field labels, always Parchment Dim, never full-strength.

cert.purpose: A slab's serial number, numeric grade, and rarity·type tag — the certificate register, deliberately colder than the serif beside it.

shadows.name: rarity-glow-common
shadows.purpose: COMMON slabs sit flush with no glow at all.

shadows.name: rarity-glow-legendary
shadows.purpose: LEGENDARY slab glow — the strongest in the system.

shadows.name: pack-glow
shadows.purpose: The sealed booster pack's own glow on the pull-reveal selection screen — a different object from a graded slab, keeps its own gift-wrap glow.

motion.name: pack-shake
motion.purpose: Pack-opening state — the pack visibly shakes while the real API call resolves underneath, minimum 1.1s so it always has room to play.

motion.name: pack-glow-pulse
motion.purpose: Paired with pack-shake — the burst glow behind the pack pulses in sync.

motion.name: hover-scale
motion.purpose: The pack-cover button's press feedback — the only scale-based micro-interaction in the system.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one primary action per screen — Molten Gold fill, near-black text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #e6af2d; color: #241a06; border: none; border-radius: 10px; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, transform 0.1s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, #e6af2d 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, #e6af2d 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action — void-black fill, hairline border.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: #0c0c0e; color: #e8e6e0; border: 1px solid #333338; border-radius: 10px; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #202024; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Slate-surface field with a gold focus border, no glow.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #202024; color: #e8e6e0; border: 1px solid #333338; border-radius: 10px; padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 14px; width: 100%; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: #e6af2d; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #87878d; }

components.name: Surface Card
components.description: The charcoal panel used for the login form, Home's balance card, and dialogs — a flat panel, not a slab.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #17171a; color: #e8e6e0; border: 1px solid #333338; border-radius: 18px; padding: 20px; }

components.name: CardArt — Graded Slab
components.description: The signature component: a colorless glassy case (padding-trick border, not border-image) topped by a dense label strip — a rarity-colored holo bar, a mono serial + grade row, the card name, and a mono rarity·type tag. Rarity color is concentrated in the strip and the GR text, not the case border. Locked cards render as an empty, dashed, label-less case.
components.html:
NO. 000042GR 8.3

Ancient Golden Dragon

LEGENDARY · CREATURE
components.css: .ds-slab { aspect-ratio: 3 / 4.2; border-radius: 10px; padding: 3px; background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(255,255,255,.24), rgba(255,255,255,.02) 45%, rgba(255,255,255,.14) 75%, rgba(255,255,255,.24)); box-shadow: 0 0 28.8px 0 color-mix(in srgb, #e6af2d 45%, transparent); } .ds-slab-inner { display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100%; width: 100%; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 7px; background: #202024; } .ds-slab-holo { height: 4px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, #e6af2d, #f0c96b, #e6af2d); } .ds-slab-row { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 4px 6px 0; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 8px; color: #87878d; } .ds-slab-grade { font-weight: 700; color: #e6af2d; } .ds-slab-name { margin: 0; padding: 0 6px; font-family: Georgia, serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; color: #e8e6e0; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-slab-tag { padding: 0 6px 4px; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 7px; letter-spacing: .05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #87878d; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-slab-art { flex: 1; background: #202024; }

narrative.overview: Owning a card is it being sealed and certified — the act of possession is the precious object, not just the art underneath. Every CardArt is a PSA/BGS-style graded slab: a glassy, colorless acrylic case (not a rarity-colored border), topped by a dense label strip carrying a thin holographic rarity band, a mono certificate serial number (the real database id of that exact exemplar), the card's name, and a numeric grade derived from its float_value. A locked (unowned) card is an empty, label-less case: a dashed outline and a lock icon, deliberately inert. This replaced an earlier 'holo-foil booster pack' treatment (full-border rarity gradient, a circular medallion, a clip-path name banner) — same void-black/molten-gold palette throughout, a confirmed brand commitment this redesign did not touch; only the material language wrapping the palette changed, from gift-wrapped to certified.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground with a single reserved gold accent, not a dark theme with several competing accents.
Rarity now lives in a concentrated holo strip and the label's GR text color, not a full-card border — the case itself stays neutral/glassy.
Every owned exemplar carries a visible mono serial number and numeric grade — no two copies of the same card are visually interchangeable.
Serif display type for headings and card names; sans for UI chrome; mono for certificate data.
No light mode. The identity only exists in dark form.

rules.name: The Reserved Gold Rule
rules.body: Molten Gold appears on the primary action and on LEGENDARY rarity — nowhere else. A second unrelated gold element on the same screen dilutes both.

rules.name: The Earned Glow Rule
rules.body: Box-shadow glow exists only as a function of rarity (0 / 9 / 16 / 24px for COMMON/RARE/EPIC/LEGENDARY). No UI element outside the rarity system gets a decorative glow.

rules.name: The Serif-Means-Precious Rule
rules.body: If the serif appears somewhere, that content is meant to feel collectible-grade. Don't reach for it on routine UI chrome (button labels, form inputs) — that dilutes the signal.

rules.name: The Cert-Is-Cold Rule
rules.body: Mono type never carries warmth or personality — it's the register for facts (a serial, a grade), never for anything the serif or sans could say instead.

rules.name: The Flat-Unless-Rare Rule
rules.body: Nothing gets a shadow by default. A shadow is always the rarity system speaking, never a generic 'card' or 'panel' affordance.

dos: Do reserve Molten Gold for the primary action and LEGENDARY rarity — never a decorative accent elsewhere on the same screen, including a GR value or a count badge on a non-legendary card.
Do let rarity be the only source of glow/shadow in the system (0/9/16/24px COMMON→LEGENDARY).
Do use the serif display face only for content that should feel collectible-grade (titles, a slab's card name) — not for buttons or form labels.
Do keep a slab's label height constant regardless of art/data availability — render the name unconditionally, gate only what genuinely has nothing to show.
Do namespace any per-exemplar generated SVG id by that exemplar's own identity, not just a locally-shifted seed, whenever more than one card can render on the same page.
donts: Don't add drop shadows for generic UI hierarchy (dropdown menus, sticky headers) — depth comes from the surface/ground contrast (Charcoal vs. Slate vs. Void), not shadows.
Don't introduce a second accent color alongside gold. Secondary/tertiary color only exists as the rarity ladder.

Don't reach for celebratory mobile-freemium patterns — confetti, toast pop-ups, badge/streak counters — even for genuinely good news (a LEGENDARY pull, a completed trade). The existing pack-shake + glow language is the ceiling for celebration.
Don't ship a light theme or a prefers-color-scheme variant. The identity is dark-only; dark: variants stay permanently inert behind a .dark class the app never applies.
Don't let a slab's own label and a nearby list (the exemplar-list modal, a duplicate-count badge) disagree on how the same rarity is colored — one RARITY_ACCENT map, never a locally hardcoded gold.
